$comment: THE RUSH PURSE — GitHub issue #372, docs/38-what-the-game-is.md § 2.3, and the owner's ruling of 2026-09-10 on that issue: a round is a sitting, posted whole; the server replays the chain and derives each round's purse from the previous round's hold moment. Parsed by packages/core/src/config/rushPurse.ts, which holds the schema and the arithmetic; packages/server reads it at boot and derives every purse from a replay. PROVENANCE, per the owner's 2026-09-08 standing ruling on governed data/ values: THE ONE FIGURE IN THIS FILE, unitsPerWaveOutlasted, IS AN AGENT'S PROPOSAL, APPROVED AS DRAFTED by the product owner on 2026-09-11 (DECISIONS.md § D542), and IT IS NOT MEASURED. Its schema bounds are chosen too. What is not chosen is the RULE the figure feeds: a round pays its purse on the waves it outlasted — a count read off the server's own replay at the hold moment (core sim/rush.ts#rushWavesOutlasted) — and on nothing else the run measured, so no wait, no carried count and no quotable mean can move a purse (docs/38 § 2.3: 'Nothing about the purse changes because time passed'; § D526 clause 2's rule applied to units). WHAT IS NOT BUILT, said here so nobody reads the purse as spendable: no between-round rebuild travels to the server yet. A rebuild is the fit-out kit (§ D427), and the code that turns a kit into a building is packages/viz/src/campaign/fitOut.ts and packages/viz/src/commissioning/, which the server may not import (§ D215 § 3). So the server derives and publishes each round's purse, and nothing can spend it — packages/server/src/leaderboard/rushSitting.ts says so where the rebuild would enter.
note: CHOSEN: 2 units a wave outlasted, the dispatcher tier's typical price in data/price-schedule.json. At that rate a round that outlasts five waves pays 10 units — about one equipment-tier change (typical 9) — and a round that outlasts ten pays 20, about one building-tier change (typical 20), which is docs/38 § 2.3's 'a player who lasts longer has more to rebuild with' as a ladder a player can read. MEASURED, and only as context for the choice rather than as its derivation: the waves a round outlasts under collective on each shipped tower as built — garden-apartments 6, midtown-office 9, crown-hotel 11, chancery-house 15, secure-tower 15, st-jude-hospital 16, mixed-use-high-rise 25, and all 30 on vertical-city and burj-class-reference, which never cross the line (RUSH_SITTING_COST_OUT=/tmp/rush-sitting-cost.md npx vitest run --project server packages/server/src/leaderboard/rushSitting.cost.test.ts, 2026-09-11). So a first round pays 12 to 50 units at this figure, and the smallest shipped tower's first round buys roughly one equipment-tier change. The purse is a balance within the sitting: it opens at whatever the listed top-up sinks bought (nothing on the standard board), each round pays into it, and it would be spent by a rebuild between rounds once one travels. CHOSEN, and stated because invariant 8 asks for it: the figure may be tuned over 1–20 units; 1 is the least a wave can pay and still be a purse, and 20 would let one wave buy a building-tier change. APPROVED AS DRAFTED by the product owner on 2026-09-11: the figure, its 1–20 schema, and the purse as a balance whose unspent units carry to the next round (DECISIONS.md § D542).
